#### Time homogeneity

Finally, we make an assumption that is specific to this example and is not part of the BRNFFRCISTG: the structural equations are identical across time points $s$, with the exception of the random variables defined for $s = 0$, each of which has no parents. Identical structural distributions (@def-identical-distributions) make equivalent variables share an equation across units, not across periods; time homogeneity pools the periods as well. 

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Structural: Places } (\mathbb{R}) \\
&   R_{0j}                   & &= f_{ R_0}( U_{ R_{0j}}) \\
&   T_{0j}                   & &= f_{ T_0}( U_{ T_{0j}})  \\
&   R_{sj}                   & &= f_{ R}( U_{ R_{sj}},   g_{VR}(\mathbf{V}_{s-1}, {[\mathbf \Psi^T_s]}_{j}) ) \\
&   T_{sj}                   & &= f_{ T}( U_{ T_{sj}},  R_{sj})                                 \\
\text{Structural: People } (\mathbb{R}) \\
&   M_{0i}                  & &=     f_{ M_0} ( U_{ M_{0i}})       \\
&   V_{0i}                  & &=     f_{ V_0}( U_{ V_{0i}})  \\
&   M_{si}                  & &=     f_{ M} ( U_{ M_{si}} ,  V_{s-1,i},    M_{s-1, i},  g_{TM}(\mathbf{T}_{s}, {\Psi}_{si}))       \\
&   V_{si}                  & &=     f_{ V}( U_{ V_{si}},  M_{si},  V_{s-1, i})                                                \\
\text{Structural: People in places } (\mathbb{R}^{1 \times q}) \\
&  {\Psi}_{0i}   & &= F_{{\mathbf \Psi_0}}(\mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{0i}})  \\
&  {\Psi}_{si}   & &= F_{{\mathbf \Psi}}(\mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{si}}, V_{s-1,i}, \Psi_{s-1,i})  \\
\end{aligned}
$$
